problem_solved: Conventional starter culture manufacturing relies on standard anaerobic fermentation methods that yield limited cell densities, lower metabolic profiles, and short storage lifespans that complicate dairy logistics.
description: An advanced manufacturing process to cultivate highly active Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus cultures under precisely modified aerobic respiratory conditions to accelerate cell growth cycles, enhance organic flavor compound profiles, and maximize structural stress tolerance boundaries.
applications: Industrial curd and yogurt manufacturing, functional probiotic food processing, starter culture production lines, commercial dairy fermentation operations, and automated food production systems.
keywords: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus, starter culture, probiotic fermentation, aerobic respiration dairy, curd manufacturing
secondary_sector: Biotechnology & Life Sciences, MedTech & Health Care, Agribusiness & Rural Economy

technology_name: IMPROVED METHOD OF FISH CURING
institution: ICAR-Central Institute of Fisheries Technology (ICAR-CIFT Cochin)
technology_type: Food Preservation / Chemical Assays & Curing Protocols
problem_solved: Traditional fish curing relies on unscientific beach drying using low-quality, contaminated salt mixtures that trigger red halophilic bacterial infestations and rapid spoilage within two months.
description: An optimized chemical preservation methodology that mandates uniform washing filters, utilizes pure salt configurations at a standardized 1:4 salt-to-fish ratio, dries product to a moisture threshold ≤ 25%, and introduces a dusting mixture containing 3 parts calcium propionate to 27 parts powdered salt.
applications: Commercial seafood export processing plants, coastal artisanal fish curing operations, sustainable packaging facilities, food microbiology laboratories, and regional agricultural extension systems.
keywords: fish curing, food preservation, calcium propionate dusting, halophilic bacteria defense, seafood processing
secondary_sector: Biotechnology & Life Sciences, Agribusiness & Rural Economy, Advanced Materials & Chemical

technology_name: PROCESS FOR PRODUCTION OF EDIBLE GRADE MARINE COLLAGEN CONCENTRATE FROM FISH FIN WASTE
institution: ICAR-Central Institute of Fisheries Technology (ICAR-CIFT Cochin)
technology_type: Food Waste Upcycling / Marine Bio-Product Extraction
problem_solved: Retail fish market waste, specifically fish fins, is commonly discarded via anti-environmental practices like land filling or direct disposal into waterways, causing severe ecological pollution while wasting high-value protein resources.
description: An environmentally friendly bio-refinery extraction process to convert discarded fish fin waste (comprising 13% to 19% protein content on a wet basis) into edible grade collagen concentrate and partially hydrolyzed collagen powder with protein concentrations exceeding 85%.
applications: Functional food and beverage formulations, anti-aging and skin health supplements, pharmaceutical joint or bone health products, and marine waste upcycling processing units.
keywords: marine collagen, fish fin waste, edible grade protein, bio-refinery extraction, waste to wealth
secondary_sector: Biotechnology & Life Sciences, MedTech & Health Care, Water, Environment & Waste Management, Consumer & Lifestyle Products, Agribusiness & Rural Economy

technology_name: MODERN AND HYGIENIC MOBILE FISH VENDING KIOSK
institution: ICAR-Central Institute of Fisheries Technology (ICAR-CIFT Cochin)
technology_type: Mobile Cold Chain Hardware / Sanitation Systems
problem_solved: Traditional street fish vendors store inventory in open, unhygienic containers using expensive melting ice, exposing highly perishable stock to severe contamination, fly infestations, and premature spoilage.
description: A cart-mounted mobile vending station structured from stainless steel (SS 304), integrating an insulated 100 kg main storage box, a 20 kg chilled holding chamber ($2\text{ to }4^\circ\text{C}$), a solar PV battery inverter subsystem, a hand-operated rotary descaling cylinder, and an integrated washbasin dressing deck.
applications: Urban street fish retail vending, smallholder fisherfolk cooperatives, mobile community retail markets, decentralized seafood distribution loops, and rural livelihood enhancement projects.
keywords: mobile fish kiosk, fish descaling machine, chilled storage vending, solar powered cart, street vendor hygiene
secondary_sector: Food Technology, Energy, Climate & Sustainability, Agribusiness & Rural Economy

technology_name: METHOD FOR PRODUCTION OF ABSORBABLE SURGICAL SUTURES FROM FISH GUT COLLAGEN
institution: ICAR-Central Institute of Fisheries Technology (ICAR-CIFT Cochin)
problem_solved: Fine-grade absorbable surgical sutures used in critical micro-surgeries and ophthalmic procedures are heavily monopolized by multinational corporations, creating high medical procurement costs (₹500 to ₹800 per suture) and limited regional accessibility.
description: A low-cost biotechnology processing method involving the extraction of intestinal guts from live fish, chemical removal of non-collagenous proteins and soluble impurities to isolate pure collagen fibers, followed by mechanical twisting, cross-linking, surface smoothening, precision sizing, and structural sterilization inside an isopropanol medium.
applications: Ophthalmic surgical interventions, clinical micro-surgeries, biomedical tissue engineering loops, wound closure hardware manufacturing, and medical grade biomaterial production lines.
keywords: surgical sutures, fish gut collagen, absorbable biomaterial, wound closure, micro-surgery hardware
secondary_sector: Advanced Materials & Chemical, MedTech & Health Care
